name: OH-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+10 district lean favors incumbent David Joyce
Joyce holds a massive cash advantage ($3.1M vs $34K)
No public polling and no expert ratings; markets price ~95% Republican
Joyce has never faced a serious general-election threat
model.rationale: The R+10 district, Joyce's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets pricing him near 95% all point to a comfortable Republican win, with no polling or outside spending suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or unexpected polling showing Jukic within single digits would be the main signal of a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican David Joyce seeks another term in this northeastern Ohio district, which leans about ten points Republican at the presidential level. He is a well-established incumbent who has won easily in past cycles and enters the fall with roughly $3.1 million on hand after raising $1.4 million. Democrat Maria Jukic has raised only about $62,000 and has minimal cash, with no outside groups engaged on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets give Joyce roughly a 95% chance of winning. With the incumbent's financial dominance, the district's partisan lean, and no evidence of a competitive environment, the forecast expects Joyce to win by a double-digit margin, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of polling.
